largest for t (3.21), then g (-0.20), then W (-0.52), then q (-1.15), then Z (-1.16); it separates t jets from the rest best (AUC 0.96: large for t)

expl.summary: Every jet is placed on 16 scales, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables (for the mass observables the if-statements could also use the offered candidate thresholds 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 times the W, Z, H and top masses, such as 80.4, 86.4, 91.19, 120.6, 160.8 and 172.8 GeV), and each class score adds some scales and subtracts others; the formula classifies 81.2% of validation jets correctly. The g score rests mainly on particle multiplicity (neuron 1: many particles with pT spread over them, +46%, and the neuron whose freezing costs the most accuracy, 12.0 points), from which the q score subtracts (-22%); the two light-parton scores are separated from the heavier jets by subtracting a scale that is off for light jets and follows low D₂ and τ₂₁ (neuron 4, -32% of the q score, -17% of the g score) and by adding a scale that is largest for light jets with high τ₂₁ and D₂ (neuron 9, +23% of the q score, +14% of the g score). The W and Z scores both subtract the wide, massive-jet scale (neuron 8, -25% and -27%) and add a scale for few particles with pT inside ΔR < 0.2 and mass below 173 GeV (neuron 5, +15% and +18%). W and Z are split by jet mass: a scale peaking at a jet mass near 78 GeV (neuron 0) raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the Z score (-20%), a compact scale for jets lighter than 92.9 GeV (neuron 11) raises the W score (+11%), while a narrow mass band near 91-101 GeV with almost all pT inside ΔR < 0.3 (neuron 7) raises the Z score (+8%) and lowers the W score (-6%), and a mass/pT window of 0.09-0.14 above about 83 GeV of mass (neuron 14) lowers the W score (-9%). The t score subtracts a total-pT scale that is switched off for heavy jets (neuron 13, -35%) and adds broad angular spread (neuron 10: large ΣzΔR, Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ and τ₁, +29%).

0.title: jet mass peaking near 78 GeV, off above about 100 GeV
0.measures: Its strongest terms are on jet mass: pushed down as the mass rises above 78.3 GeV (its strongest term), above 92.9 GeV and above 74.3 GeV, partly restored above 91.19 GeV (an offered candidate threshold), and pushed down for jets lighter than 101 GeV (mass < 101.05, more the lighter the jet), so it rises with mass up to about 74-78 GeV and falls above; jets heavier than about 100 GeV are at zero. It is pushed up for small mass/pT (mass/pT squared < 0.00787 and < 0.00694) and down for very small ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² (< 0.00617); overall it falls with mass, mass/pT and λ₁+λ₂ (rank correlations -0.667, -0.644, -0.644), because the heaviest jets sit at zero. W jets sit highest (1.64), then quarks (0.69), gluons (0.40) and Z jets (0.29), with tops lowest (0.09). It is zero for 1.5% of W jets, 20.3% of quarks, 31.7% of Z jets, 47.3% of gluons and 90.8% of tops.
0.role: It raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the Z score (-20%), so it separates jets near 78 GeV from those near 91 GeV and heavier. It hardly enters the t score (+2%) and does not enter the g or q scores.

1.title: many particles, pT spread over many of them
1.measures: It follows the number of particles (rank correlation 0.663), the number of particles above 1 GeV (0.64) and falls with the pT share of the 40 hardest particles (-0.624). Its strongest terms: pushed down when the softest particle has pT < 2.28 GeV (0 if the jet has at most 15 particles) and pushed up for pT < 1.52 GeV of that particle, pushed up for high total pT (log of total pT > 6.89 and > 6.91, pushed down for < 7.14), for τ₁ < 0.195, for pT entropy > 2.07 and for more than 38 particles, and pushed down when the 50 hardest particles carry more than 95.9% of the pT. Gluons sit far highest (5.86), then tops (2.91), quarks (2.16), Z (1.67) and W jets (1.62). It is almost never zero (0.1% of gluons, 0.7% of tops, 8.4% of quarks, 9.2% of Z and 9.6% of W jets).
1.role: It raises the g score, where it is the largest input (+46%), and lowers the q score (-22%), so it separates gluons from quarks by multiplicity. It does not enter the W, Z or t scores. Freezing it costs 12.0 accuracy points, the most of any neuron.

2.title: high total jet pT, compact hard core
2.measures: It follows the total pT (rank correlation 0.652) and the pT of the 50 hardest particles (0.624). Its strongest term pushes it down for jets lighter than 92.9 GeV, partly undone below 91.19 GeV; it is pushed up for log of total pT > 6.90 combined with a compact core of the 15 hardest particles (ΣzΔR² < 0.0215), and for total pT > 1017 GeV, and pushed down for total pT < 1261 GeV. Gluons sit highest (0.57), then Z (0.21) and W jets (0.18), quarks (0.12) and tops (0.05); it is zero for 32.9% of gluons, 54.5% of Z, 63.0% of W, 77.6% of quarks and 85.4% of tops.
2.role: It lowers the Z score slightly (-2%) and does not enter the g, W or t scores; its effect on the classification is small (freezing it changes accuracy by -0.03 points).

3.title: few particles, thin jet (small λ₂, τ₃, τ₄)
3.measures: It falls with the smaller eigenvalue λ₂ (rank correlation -0.784), τ₄ (-0.751), τ₃ (-0.735) and the number of particles (-0.726). Its strongest terms are on ΣzΔR²: pushed down for ΣzΔR² < 0.00961 and up for ΣzΔR² of the 40 hardest particles < 0.00884; it is pushed down for D₂ < 2.41 but pushed up when D₂ < 2.41 and D₂ (β = 2) < 5.14 together, pushed up for fewer than 46 particles and for λ₂ < 0.000615, and pushed down for τ₂₁ < 0.386. W jets sit highest (0.78), then quarks (0.61) and Z jets (0.48), with gluons (0.15) and tops (0.03) low; it is zero for 7.3% of W jets, 22.1% of quarks, 25.6% of Z, 48.4% of gluons and 91.2% of tops.
3.role: It raises the W score (+4%) and the Z score (+4%) and lowers the g score (-8%), where gluons, with more particles, sit low. It does not enter the q or t scores.

4.title: off for light jets, low D₂ and τ₂₁
4.measures: Built from jet-mass steps: pushed down for jets lighter than 86.4 GeV (its strongest term), 92.9 GeV and 78.3 GeV, pushed up for mass < 101.05 GeV and < 120.6 GeV, and pushed down when the 40 hardest particles have mass < 163.3 GeV, so it is off for light jets and on for most jets heavier than about 78 GeV; it is also pushed up for ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² > 0.0096 and for fewer than 26 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4, and pushed down for more than 22 particles; for the heaviest, widest jets ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² > 0.0096 keeps it on. It falls with D₂ (β = 2) (rank correlation -0.697), D₂ (-0.693) and τ₂₁ (β = 2) (-0.677) and rises with the mass of the 10 hardest particles (0.655). Z jets sit highest (1.46), then W (1.18) and tops (0.74), with gluons (0.16) and quarks (0.10) low; it is zero for 83.2% of quarks and 65.5% of gluons, but only for 8.7-11.6% of W, Z and top jets.
4.role: It lowers the q score, where it is the largest input (-32%), and the g score (-17%), and raises the W score (+6%) and the t score (+4%). It does not enter the Z score.

5.title: few particles, pT inside ΔR < 0.2, jet mass below 173 GeV
5.measures: Many of its terms are on total pT and partly cancel: pushed up for pT of the 50 hardest particles > 934 and > 959 GeV and for total pT > 908 GeV, pushed down for total pT > 986 GeV and log of total pT > 6.91 and > 6.92. On mass it is pushed up above 74.3 GeV and for groomed (soft-drop) mass above 69.7 GeV, and pushed down above 172.8 GeV, for mass of the 50 hardest particles above 157.5 GeV, for mass/pT > 0.077 and for max ΔR > 0.240. It falls with the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlation -0.617), the number of particles (-0.608) and λ₂ (-0.605), and rises with the pT share within ΔR < 0.2 (0.568). Z jets sit highest (1.72), then W (1.47) and quarks (1.40), with gluons (0.52) and tops (0.29) low; it is zero for 0.4% of Z, 0.7% of W, 7.8% of quarks, 28.9% of gluons and 66.2% of tops.
5.role: It raises the Z score (+18%) and the W score (+15%) and lowers the t score (-13%) and the g score (-9%). It does not enter the q score.

6.title: high D₂ and τ₂₁, small e₂, many soft-drop removals
6.measures: Its strongest term pushes it up when the 50 hardest particles have mass < 172.8 GeV (and down below 169.0 GeV); on jet mass it is pushed down below 101.05 and 120.6 GeV and up below 92.9 and 86.4 GeV, and it is pushed up for mass/pT > 0.0268 and down for mass/pT > 0.098. It rises with D₂ (β = 2) (rank correlation 0.477), the number of branches removed by soft drop (0.469) and τ₂₁ (β = 2) (0.46), and falls with e₂ (-0.468). Quarks sit highest (1.18), then gluons (0.78) and tops (0.39); W and Z jets sit at 0.10 and are zero for 87.1% and 85.6% of them (gluons 19.9%, quarks 11.1%, tops 54.2%).
6.role: It lowers the Z score (-12%) and raises the q score (+5%) and the g score (+2%). It does not enter the W or t scores.

7.title: narrow jet-mass band near 91-101 GeV, pT within ΔR < 0.3
7.measures: Built from products of a jet-mass condition (mass < 91.19, 92.9, 101.05 or 82.9 GeV) with the pT share within ΔR < 0.3 of the axis (above 0.964, 0.978 or 0.998). Terms with neighbouring mass thresholds enter with opposite signs (mass < 91.19 with share > 0.964 pushes up, mass < 92.9 with share > 0.964 pushes down; mass < 91.19 with share > 0.978 pushes down, mass < 101.05 with share > 0.978 pushes up), so the neuron responds to jets whose mass lies in the narrow bands between these thresholds and that have almost all their pT within ΔR < 0.3. It falls with the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlation -0.464) and rises with the pT share within ΔR < 0.3 (0.436). Z jets sit far highest (1.53); quarks (0.14), W (0.10), gluons (0.08) and tops (0.06) are near zero. It is zero for 13.6% of Z jets, but for 50.7% of quarks, 60.5% of W, 74.3% of gluons and 86.5% of tops.
7.role: It raises the Z score (+8%) and lowers the W score (-6%) and the t score (-3%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

8.title: wide, massive jet (large λ₁+λ₂, ΣzΔR², mass/pT)
8.measures: It rises with mass/pT, λ₁+λ₂, ΣzΔR² and ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² (rank correlation 0.701 each) and falls with the pT share within ΔR < 0.2 (-0.697). Its strongest term pushes it down for narrow jets (λ₁+λ₂ < 0.00961); it is pushed up for mass above 64.5, 74.3 and 87.4 GeV and down above 101.05 GeV, pushed up when mass/pT > 0.077 with total pT < 1116 GeV, and pushed down when the 50 hardest particles have mass > 82.0 GeV, when fewer than 39 particles carry 90% of the pT and when more than 7 do. Tops sit far highest (3.58), then gluons (1.45) and quarks (0.59), with Z (0.25) and W jets (0.05) lowest; it is zero for 3.8% of tops, 34.1% of gluons, 50.7% of Z, 70.7% of quarks and 88.7% of W jets.
8.role: It lowers the Z score (-27%) and the W score (-25%), where it is the largest input of both, and raises the t score (+6%). It hardly enters the g or q scores.

9.title: jet mass well below 80 GeV, high τ₂₁ and D₂
9.measures: Almost entirely a function of jet mass: pushed down for mass < 160.8 GeV (its strongest term) and < 143.8 GeV, pushed up for mass < 162.8 GeV and < 172.8 GeV (160.8 and 172.8 GeV are offered candidate thresholds), pushed up when the 50 hardest particles have mass < 138.9 GeV, plus small terms at 82.9 and 92.9 GeV. The large opposing terms nearly cancel, and the net result is largest for light jets, near zero for jets of about 80-92 GeV, and small but non-zero again for heavier jets. It rises with τ₂₁ (β = 2) (rank correlation 0.664), D₂ (β = 2) (0.655), τ₂₁ (0.642) and planar flow (0.606) and falls with 1−λ₂/λ₁ (-0.606). Quarks sit highest (2.35), then gluons (1.60) and tops (0.60), with W (0.30) and Z jets (0.21) low; it is zero for 89.1% of Z, 70.0% of W, 30.0% of tops, 17.2% of gluons and 10.7% of quarks.
9.role: It raises the q score (+23%) and the g score (+14%) and lowers the W score (-5%). It does not enter the Z or t scores.

10.title: broad angular spread (large ΣzΔR, Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½, τ₁)
10.measures: It rises with Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (rank correlation 0.746), τ₁ (0.744) and ΣzΔR (0.744) and falls with the pT share within ΔR < 0.05 (-0.724). Its strongest terms: pushed down for ΣzΔR < 0.121 and up for τ₁ < 0.151; on mass, pushed down above 64.5 GeV and up above 78.3 GeV, up below 89.7 GeV and down below 101.05 GeV; pushed up for e₂ > 0.0126 and down when the harder of two subjets has mass < 65.2 GeV. Tops sit highest (2.40), then Z (0.96), W (0.93), gluons (0.87) and quarks (0.56); it is zero for 3.7% of tops, 15.9% of Z, 16.6% of W, 33.6% of gluons and 56.6% of quarks.
10.role: It raises the t score (+29%), its second-largest input. It hardly enters the g and q scores and does not enter the W or Z scores. Freezing it costs 2.39 accuracy points.

11.title: compact jet below 93 GeV of mass, few particles
11.measures: Its strongest term pushes it up for mass < 92.9 GeV (and for mass of the 50 hardest particles < 97.9 GeV); it is pushed down for masses below 80.4 GeV (an offered candidate threshold) and for mass of the 50 hardest particles < 80.4 GeV. It is pushed down for the narrowest jets (ΣzΔR < 0.0768, λ₁ < 0.00672) but up for ΣzΔR < 0.0859, ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² < 0.00818 and e₂ < 0.0303, and up when more than 99.0% of the pT is within ΔR < 0.3. It falls with λ₂ (rank correlation -0.741), the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (-0.688), τ₄ (-0.682) and the number of particles (-0.676). W jets sit highest (1.57), then Z (0.91) and quarks (0.76), with gluons (0.39) and tops (0.13) low; it is zero for 2.4% of W, 8.9% of Z, 14.9% of quarks, 36.1% of gluons and 74.0% of tops.
11.role: It raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the q score (-8%). It does not enter the g, Z or t scores.

12.title: jet mass below about 83 GeV, rising as the mass falls
12.measures: Its strongest term pushes it up for mass < 82.9 GeV, together with mass < 74.3 GeV and mass < 86.4 GeV combined with λ₂ < 0.00369; it is partly pulled back for the lightest jets (mass < 62.55 GeV, an offered candidate threshold, and < 53.9 GeV), for a very compact core (ΣzΔR² of the 15 hardest particles < 0.00614) and for mass/pT < 0.069. It falls with mass (rank correlation -0.634) and with λ₁+λ₂ and ΣzΔR² (-0.618). Quarks sit highest (1.44), then gluons (0.58) and W jets (0.29), with Z (0.11) and tops (0.08) low; it is zero for 23.3% of quarks, 39.6% of W, 55.9% of gluons, 80.8% of tops and 92.2% of Z jets.
12.role: It raises the q score (+7%), the Z score (+4%) and the g score (+3%), and lowers the W score (-5%) and the t score (-5%).

13.title: total jet pT, switched off for heavy or wide jets
13.measures: It rises with the total pT (rank correlation 0.591) and the number of particles (a linear term). Its strongest term pushes it down for small mass/pT (mass/pT squared < 0.0258); it is pushed up when ΣzΔR² of the 50 hardest particles is < 0.0255 (also combined with more than 96.4% of the pT within ΔR < 0.3), and pushed down for heavy jets: mass of the 40 hardest particles < 160.8 GeV, mass above 101.05 and 143.8 GeV, and mass above 172.8 GeV together with soft particles present. Z jets sit highest (1.99), then W (1.83), gluons (1.78) and quarks (1.39); tops sit lowest (0.69) and are zero for 42.2% of them (Z 0.5%, W 0.6%, quarks 8.7%, gluons 15.5%).
13.role: It lowers the t score, where it is the largest input (-35%). It does not enter the g, q, W or Z scores.

14.title: jet mass above about 83-91 GeV, mass/pT 0.09-0.14
14.measures: Its strongest terms push it down for jets lighter than 82.9 GeV, 89.7 GeV and 91.19 GeV (an offered candidate threshold) and for mass of the 50 hardest particles < 97.9 GeV, and push it up below 125.1 GeV; on mass/pT it is pushed up below 0.141, 0.118 and 0.098 and down below 0.0905, so it is on for mass/pT of about 0.09-0.14. It is pushed down for the narrowest jets (λ₁ < 0.00824, ΣzΔR² of the 30 hardest particles < 0.00258). It rises weakly with mass (rank correlation 0.352). Z jets sit far highest (0.93); gluons (0.18), tops (0.13), quarks (0.08) and W jets (0.03) are near zero. It is zero for 15.0% of Z jets, 65.4% of tops, 72.4% of gluons, 88.4% of W and 88.5% of quarks.
14.role: It lowers the W score (-9%), so it separates Z jets, heavier than the 83-91 GeV thresholds, from W jets. It does not enter the g, q, Z or t scores.

15.title: narrow jet with pT in the core, small soft-drop angle
15.measures: Its strongest term pushes it down for a soft-drop splitting angle < 0.302 (pushed up again below 0.204); it is pushed up for log of total pT < 7.02, ΣzΔR < 0.0859, soft-drop mass < 79.2 GeV and ΣzΔR² of the 5 and 10 hardest particles < 0.00833 and < 0.00768, and pushed down when the pT share within ΔR < 0.2 exceeds 0.871 and for e₂ > 0.0303. It rises with the pT share within ΔR < 0.05 (rank correlation 0.549) and falls with the pT share at 0.1 ≤ ΔR < 0.2 (-0.588), Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (-0.544) and ΣzΔR (-0.537). Quarks sit highest (0.58), then W (0.44), Z (0.43) and gluons (0.34), with tops lowest (0.09); it is zero for 21.7% of quarks, 40.5% of W, 42.2% of gluons, 61.6% of Z and 85.8% of tops.
15.role: It raises the Z score (+5%) and lowers the t score (-4%). It hardly enters the W score (-2%) and does not enter the g or q scores.

g.title: gluon: many particles, not two-prong
g.measures: High for jets with many particles and no two-prong structure: it rises with N₂ (rank correlation 0.691), τ₂₁ (β = 2) (0.673) and planar flow (0.648) and falls with 1−λ₂/λ₁ (-0.648). It averages 3.28 for g jets, 1.04 for q and 0.44 for t, and is negative for W (-1.92) and Z (-2.07) (AUC 0.93 for gluons against the rest).
g.built_from: Mostly adds multiplicity (neuron 1, +46%) and the light-jet scale with high τ₂₁ (neuron 9, +14%); subtracts the low-D₂ scale that is off for light jets (neuron 4, -17%), the few-particles scale with mass below 173 GeV (neuron 5, -9%) and the thin few-particle scale (neuron 3, -8%); adds a little of neurons 12 (+3%) and 6 (+2%).

q.title: light quark: few particles, one-prong, light
q.measures: High for jets with high D₂ and τ₂₁ (rank correlations 0.701 for D₂ with β = 2, 0.688 for τ₂₁ with β = 2, 0.663 for D₂). It averages 2.75 for q jets and 1.34 for g (gluons are its main confusion), 0.47 for t, and is negative for W (-0.29) and Z (-0.54) (AUC 0.90).
q.built_from: Subtracts the low-D₂ scale that is off for light jets (neuron 4, -32%) and multiplicity (neuron 1, -22%), and the compact below-93-GeV scale (neuron 11, -8%); adds the light-jet scale with high τ₂₁ (neuron 9, +23%), the below-83-GeV mass scale (neuron 12, +7%) and a little of neuron 6 (+5%).

W.title: W: compact jet, mass near 78 GeV
W.measures: High for compact jets with few particles and a mass near 78 GeV; it falls with mass, mass/pT, λ₁+λ₂ and ΣzΔR² over all jets (rank correlations about -0.65), since massive wide jets are pushed far down. It averages 3.43 for W jets and 0.33 for q, is near zero for Z (-0.06), and negative for g (-1.12) and t (-2.84) (AUC 0.97).
W.built_from: Subtracts the wide, massive-jet scale (neuron 8, -25%, its largest input); adds the few-particles scale with mass below 173 GeV (neuron 5, +15%), the mass-peak scale near 78 GeV (neuron 0, +11%) and the compact below-93-GeV scale (neuron 11, +11%), plus neurons 4 (+6%) and 3 (+4%); subtracts the mass/pT 0.09-0.14 window above 83-91 GeV (neuron 14, -9%), the 91-101 GeV narrow band (neuron 7, -6%) and a little of neurons 9 and 12 (-5% each).

Z.title: Z: compact jet with few particles, heavier than 78 GeV
Z.measures: High for jets with few particles and small λ₂, τ₃ and τ₄ (rank correlations -0.609 with τ₄, -0.607 with λ₂, -0.605 with the number of particles). It averages 3.24 for Z jets, 0.43 for q and 0.31 for W, and is negative for g (-1.02) and t (-2.55) (AUC 0.96).
Z.built_from: Subtracts the wide, massive-jet scale (neuron 8, -27%) and the mass-peak scale near 78 GeV (neuron 0, -20%), which separates it from W jets, and the high-D₂ scale (neuron 6, -12%); adds the few-particles scale with mass below 173 GeV (neuron 5, +18%), the 91-101 GeV narrow band (neuron 7, +8%), the narrow-core scale (neuron 15, +5%) and a little of neurons 3 and 12 (+4% each); subtracts a little of neuron 2 (-2%).

t.title: top: broad, massive jet
t.measures: High for broad jets: it rises with ΣzΔR and τ₁ (rank correlation 0.777 each), Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (0.768) and mass/pT (0.73). It averages 3.21 for t jets and is negative for all others: g (-0.20), W (-0.52), q (-1.15) and Z (-1.16) (AUC 0.96).
t.built_from: Subtracts the total-pT scale that is switched off for heavy jets (neuron 13, -35%, its largest input) and adds broad angular spread (neuron 10, +29%); subtracts the few-particles scale with mass below 173 GeV (neuron 5, -13%) and a little of neurons 12 (-5%), 15 (-4%) and 7 (-3%); adds a little of the wide, massive-jet scale (neuron 8, +6%) and of neuron 4 (+4%).

0.name: jets of about 79 GeV, narrow, pT at ΔR 0.05-0.1
0.jets: Mostly W (71%) with g 9%, t 7%, q 7%, Z 6%; 24.5% of all jets. Mean mass 79.1 GeV, λ₁+λ₂ 0.0061, total pT 1023 GeV (all jets: 89.9 GeV, 0.0093, 1044 GeV); leading particle 241.73 GeV; 35% of the pT lies at ΔR 0.05-0.1 from the axis (all jets: 27%).
0.why: mass < 101 always passes and adds -0.717; (m/ΣpT)² < 0.00787 passes for 97% and adds +0.6; n(0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4) < 15 passes for 94% and adds +0.455; ΣpT(50 hardest) < 1.16e+03 passes for 97% and adds +0.453. Of the neuron's main terms, mass > 92.9 never passes here. The steps above 74.3 and 78.3 GeV take little because the mass sits just above them; mass < 101 is the main penalty. The neuron averages 1.473 and is on for 94%, adding +1.104 to the W score, -2.025 to the Z score, +0.184 to the t score; the formula calls them W (right for 82%).

1.name: jets of about 91 GeV, pT at ΔR 0.05-0.1
1.jets: Mostly Z (76%) with g 9%, t 8%; 22.1% of all jets. Mean mass 91.2 GeV, λ₁+λ₂ 0.0079, total pT 1036 GeV (all jets: 89.9 GeV, 0.0093, 1044 GeV); leading particle 240.19 GeV; 41% of the pT lies at ΔR 0.05-0.1 from the axis (all jets: 27%).
1.why: mass > 78.3 always passes and adds -1.632; mass > 74.3 always passes and adds -0.519; ΣpT(50 hardest) < 1.16e+03 passes for 95% and adds +0.424; n(0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4) < 15 passes for 91% and adds +0.424. Of the neuron's main terms, mass > 92.9 passes for only 23% here. At this mass the steps above 74.3 and 78.3 GeV take much more than for the 79 GeV group. The neuron averages 0.154 and is on for 52%, adding +0.116 to the W score, -0.212 to the Z score, +0.019 to the t score; the formula calls them Z (right for 88%).

2.name: light pencil-thin jets (34 GeV), pT within ΔR 0.025
2.jets: Mostly q (64%) with g 25%, W 5%, Z 5%; 16.9% of all jets. Mean mass 33.9 GeV, λ₁+λ₂ 0.0011, total pT 1057 GeV (all jets: 89.9 GeV, 0.0093, 1044 GeV); leading particle 327.22 GeV; 87% of the pT lies at ΔR 0-0.025 from the axis (all jets: 29%).
2.why: (m/ΣpT)² < 0.00694 always passes and adds +2.464; ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² < 0.00617 always passes and adds -2.206; mass < 101 always passes and adds -2.194; (m/ΣpT)² < 0.00787 always passes and adds +2.169. Of the neuron's main terms, mass > 78.3 never passes and mass > 92.9 never passes here.
